historical_events.description: Discovered by Christopher Columbus in 1494
Conquered from Spain by British forces
Discovered by Christopher Columbus, first landing in the New World
Leeward Islands constituted as single Federal Colony by Imperial Parliament Act 34 & 35 Vict., cap. 107
Discovered by the Portuguese
First occupied by the Dutch, named Mauritius in honour of Prince Maurice
Taken possession of by the French, first on behalf of French East India Company, later (1767) for Crown of France
Captured by British forces in expedition
Possession confirmed to England by Treaty of Paris
Discovered by Vasco da Gama on Christmas Day, hence the name Natal (Portuguese for Christmas)

Langalibalele, chief of Amalubi Tribe, entered contumacious course leading to attempted escape to Basutoland. Colonial force dispatched, chief captured and tried under native law, condemned to banishment for life

Zulu War - Natal became base of hostile operations against Zulu kingdom. Major engagements included Isandhlwana (22 Jan), Rorke's Drift (22 Jan), Inyezane (22 Jan), Kambula (29 Mar), Ginginhllovu (3 Apr), and Ulundi (4 July). Cetywayo captured 28 August, kingdom restructured by Sir Garnet Wolseley 1 September
Cetywayo re-installed by Sir Theophilus Shepstone over part of former kingdom, subject to conditions, after visiting England and accepting terms of restoration
Discovered by John Cabot
Responsible Government established, last of North American colonies to receive it
Ceded to Great Britain by native chiefs
Charter granted to Sierra Leone Company
Colony transferred back to the Crown after 7 years of Company rule
Discovered by Christopher Columbus on his third voyage

Royal cedula issued by Court of Madrid offering extraordinary advantages to foreigners to settle in Trinidad, sole condition being profession of Roman Catholic religion. Led to large influx of population
Captured by British expedition under Rear-Admiral Harvey and Sir Ralph Abercrombie, articles of capitulation signed with Spanish Governor Chacon
Finally ceded to Crown of Great Britain by Treaty of Amiens
Discovered by Columbus 1498, contested by British, Dutch, French, Duke of Courland. Finally ceded to Britain in perpetuity 1814 after multiple captures and treaties
Riots occurred in Windward District. 42 persons indicted for murder, 16 sentenced to death, all reprieved and sentenced to various terms of penal servitude. Led to reorganization of Police Force
Discovered by Columbus during his fourth voyage
H.R.H. the Duke of Kent, father of Queen Victoria, placed British colours on principal fortress upon surrender to British arms
Discovered by Christopher Columbus
Violent eruption of Soufrière volcanic mountain, celebrated for its violence
5,080 Caribs embarked at Bequia and sailed for island of Rattan in Bay of Honduras, following their surrender after protracted war

notes: This extraction covers approximately 34 colony files from the 1883 Colonial Office List
Data includes comprehensive geographic, economic, demographic, and administrative information
All historical spellings and terminology preserved as in original documents
Economic data primarily covers the period 1872-1881 where available
Population data primarily from 1881 census where available
Some larger colonies (Canada, Cape of Good Hope, Australian colonies, New Zealand) were only partially extracted due to file size
Currency notations preserved as in original (£ for pounds sterling, Rs. for Rupees, $ for dollars)
All measurements preserved in imperial units as in original documents
Colonial administrative structures reflect 1883 constitutional arrangements
